Brahmin’s blessing.description: A gesture or ritual blessing given by a Brahmin, considered auspicious.

orderlies.description: Assistants or attendants, often in a court or hospital setting.

maces.description: Ceremonial staffs or clubs carried as symbols of authority.

sheriff.description: An official responsible for enforcing the law and maintaining order in the court.

Chup.description: A Hindi/Bengali word meaning 'be quiet' or 'silence'.

Hish.description: An onomatopoeic exclamation used to hush or shoo people.

penal settlement.description: A remote colony or prison where convicts are sent for punishment, often for life.

Valmiki.description: The legendary Sanskrit poet who authored the original Ramayana.

Vedas.description: Ancient sacred scriptures of Hinduism, regarded as the foundation of religious knowledge.

Puranas.description: A genre of ancient Indian texts containing mythological and historical narratives.

Haridwar.description: A holy city in northern India, significant as a pilgrimage site for Hindus.

Muhammad Shah.description: The Mughal emperor of India during Nadir Shah's invasion.

Hamir raga.description: A classical Indian musical mode or melody, often performed in vocal or instrumental music.

Norchandri.description: A traditional Bengali song or musical style, referenced as a type of song sung by Becharam Babu.

Babla.description: A type of flower, likely the babul or acacia, referenced in a song.

laba-laba.description: An onomatopoeic Bengali expression implying meaningless chatter or babbling.

puffed rice cakes.description: A traditional Bengali snack made from puffed rice, often sweetened or flavored.

Alami.description: Refers to an author whose book is mentioned in the opening conversation; likely a fictional or contemporary writer.

vakalatnama.description: A legal document in India authorizing a lawyer to represent someone in court.

Hanuman.description: A revered Hindu deity, known for his strength and devotion, central to the Ramayana.

Lanka.description: The kingdom ruled by Ravana in the Ramayana, often identified with present-day Sri Lanka.

ferryman.description: A person who operates a boat to transport people across a river.

bolster.description: A long, thick pillow used for support while reclining.

Alya.description: A character who weeps as the family departs Mathura, showing deep affection for them.

Benares.description: Another name for Varanasi/Kashi, a major pilgrimage city.

Yamuna.description: A sacred river in northern India, closely associated with Krishna and Vrindavan.

Braj.description: A cultural and religious region around Mathura and Vrindavan, associated with Krishna.

veena.description: A classical Indian stringed musical instrument.

arati.description: A Hindu ritual of worship involving the waving of lighted lamps before deities.

Manikarnika Ghat.description: A famous cremation and bathing ghat on the Ganges in Varanasi.

Dvivedis.description: A Brahmin sub-caste or title meaning 'knower of two Vedas'.

Chaturvedis.description: A Brahmin sub-caste or title meaning 'knower of four Vedas'.

Ramats.description: Likely a reference to a religious sect or group, possibly Ramats (followers of Rama).

Naimats.description: Likely refers to a sect or group, possibly related to Naimisharanya, a sacred forest.

Shaivas.description: Followers of Shiva, one of the principal Hindu sects.

Shaktas.description: Followers of Shakti, the divine feminine, a major Hindu sect.

Agni.description: The Vedic god of fire, central to Hindu rituals.

Hara Vishweshwar.description: An epithet for Shiva, the 'Lord of the Universe'.

Bhairava.description: A fierce manifestation of Shiva, worshipped in certain sects.

Udasis.description: A religious order of ascetics, often associated with Sikhism and Hinduism.

rechaka.description: A yogic breathing technique involving exhalation.

puraka.description: A yogic breathing technique involving inhalation.

kumbhaka.description: A yogic breathing technique involving breath retention.

rabab.description: A stringed instrument used in Indian and Central Asian music.

dhrupad.description: A genre of Indian classical vocal music.

dharu.description: A type of musical composition or rhythm, likely regional.

khayal.description: A style of Indian classical singing.

prabandha.description: An ancient form of Indian musical composition.

chhanda.description: A metrical pattern or rhythm in poetry and music.

sorabandha.description: Likely a type of musical composition or form.

sargam.description: Singing the notes of a scale in Indian music (sa, re, ga, ma, etc.).

chaturang.description: A genre of Indian classical music combining four elements.

naqsh.description: A term possibly referring to a musical or poetic form.

Bhagirathi.description: Another name for the Ganges river, especially in its upper reaches.

Monghyr.description: A town in Bihar, India, known for its historical and religious significance.

Navadwip.description: A holy town in Bengal, famous as the birthplace of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

Mahadev.description: A name for Shiva, meaning 'Great God'.

sadhu.description: A holy man or ascetic in Hinduism.

bangle-seller.description: A person who sells bangles, often a woman who sings songs to attract customers.

tappa.description: A form of semi-classical Indian vocal music, known for its fast, intricate passages.

jalgoja.description: A type of Bengali sweet or fried snack.

tajpheni.description: A kind of sweet or fried snack, possibly a local or regional delicacy.

ghyaaru.description: A Bengali snack or sweet, typically fried.
